# Practice Runtime V2 contract closure

This closure records the owner-authorized additive contract extension at SHA-256
`6a2b537ba1f6d0a1272898678245723b37eed83185b17b7de4f3ff02e8ae5958`.
The contracts below are additive, versioned extensions. Their implementation
and evidence are recorded in this file and the focused tests named below.

## RESOLVED — Planner readiness reconciliation

Planner now owns a private, internal-token-protected
`POST /practice-learning-routes/{routeID}/steps/{stepID}/readiness-reconciliations`
contract. Request `practice-learning-readiness-reconcile.v1` binds the exact
TaskInstance, Student, revision and digest, immutable route and digest, and step.
Planner reads current Student mastery through its existing Student adapter and
returns `practice-learning-readiness-receipt.v1` with `READY` or `NOT_READY`, a
learner-state digest, mastery-policy version, and observation time. The receipt
is persisted by Planner under an idempotency key. Same-key/same-payload calls
replay the original receipt; changed payload under that key conflicts.

Runtime exposes
`POST /api/v2/task-instances/{instanceID}/steps/{stepID}/readiness-reconciliations`
to the authenticated Student. It sends the frozen identity to Planner, verifies
the complete echoed identity, persists the receipt and replay key with that
step, and changes `LEARNING_REQUIRED` to `AVAILABLE` only for Planner's `READY`
decision. Runtime never evaluates learning completion or mastery itself.

Coverage: Planner `TestReconcileReadinessUsesCurrentStudentMasteryAndReturnsIdempotentReceipt`
and `TestReconcileReadinessRejectsWrongInstanceOrRevision`; Runtime
`TestReconcileStepReadinessUsesPlannerReceiptAndPersistsMonotonicTransition`,
`TestReconcileStepReadinessRejectsWrongPlannerIdentityAndKeyReuse`, the Planner
HTTP adapter test, strict Runtime HTTP request test, and the PostgreSQL
readiness-persistence test.

## RESOLVED — minimal learner execution projection

New Catalog publications freeze each selected milestone's authored
`execution_spec` (`practice-step-execution-spec.v1`) with `deliverables` from
`config_json.practice_execution`. Runtime maps the exact revision's milestone
title, description, acceptance checklist, and execution spec into its own
Step model. Its materialization response is
`practice-task-step-materialization.v2` and contains only the fields used by
the current Practice V2 client: instance/revision/step identity, title,
objective, deliverables, and acceptance. Dependencies, effort estimates, and
assistance policy are not required or projected. Private evaluation fields are
excluded from Step and materialization responses.

Missing or invalid authored execution specs fail closed before Start. The
frontend validates the strict v2 DTO and rejects added private fields.

Coverage: Catalog publication tests assert the versioned authored projection;
Runtime `TestProjectPublishedRevisionRequiresVersionedExecutionSpecAndProjectsAcceptanceChecklist`
asserts mapping and fail-closed behavior; the learner Step serialization test
and Next.js `practiceV2DtoSchema.test.ts` assert that private fields do not
cross the boundary.

## RESOLVED — authoritative task type

New Catalog publications require an explicit supported
`blueprint_json.classification.task_type` and freeze it at the runtime-context
top level with `task_type_schema=practice-task-type.v1` and
`execution_projection_schema=practice-task-runtime-projection.v2`. Runtime
validates the closed enum and uses only this field for its revision summary.
It does not derive task type from topology, title, prose, or steps.

Historical revision JSON is returned exactly as stored and is never backfilled.
A historical revision without the new fields remains readable by exact ID but
cannot start a new Practice V2 TaskInstance; a corrected publication creates a
new immutable revision.

Coverage: Catalog `TestPublishPracticeTaskRevisionRequiresExplicitTaskTypeAndExecutionFields`
and exact-envelope immutability tests; Runtime
`TestProjectPublishedRevisionRejectsMissingOrUnsupportedTaskType` and the
successful frozen-projection test.
